issues.description: setuptools<82 cap leaks from CI workaround into core package's runtime install_requires
issues.detail: The pkg_resources removal in setuptools 82 breaks mmcv's build, not autogluon runtime. Pinning setuptools<82 in core/setup.py forces every downstream user to inherit a CI-only build constraint at install time. The cap belongs in CI scripts and build-system requirements, not the published wheel. Move it out.

issues.description: mmengine downgrade from pinned git SHA to 0.10.7 silently drops stated torch 2.5 fix rationale
issues.detail: The prior mmengine git SHA was explicitly carrying a torch 2.5 fix. The PR switches to PyPI 0.10.7 with no comment establishing that release contains that fix. A reader cannot verify the torch 2.5 support invariant without external archaeology, and if 0.10.7 lacks the fix this trades one failure for another.

issues.description: --no-build-isolation makes setuptools cap ordering an implicit load-bearing invariant
issues.detail: Disabling build isolation means mmcv's build uses the ambient env's setuptools, which is why the prior pip install setuptools<82 must execute first. The time-ordering is implicit and the FIXME names only the symptom. Reordering or splitting these lines would break the build confusingly. State the coupling in a comment.

issues.description: FIXME comments lack a revert checklist or recipe
issues.detail: Both FIXMEs reference mmcv issue 3325 but neither enumerates what to undo: restore mim install, drop setuptools cap in build_pkg, drop cap in core/setup.py, drop --no-build-isolation, and restore the mmengine SHA pin. A short checklist or revert recipe makes eventual cleanup a mechanical edit rather than a forensic exercise.

issues.description: Same setuptools<82 workaround duplicated across three files with no single source of truth
issues.detail: The cap lives in build_pkg env_setup.sh, setup_mmcv.sh, and core/setup.py. The mm* version matrix lives only in setup_mmcv.sh. When upstream fixes the issue, the revert requires hunting three places. Consolidate to one named constant or one script to keep rollback cheap.

issues.description: Three unrelated changes bundled with empty PR description
issues.detail: build_pkg setuptools cap, mmcv install rewrite, and core install_requires change are three separate concerns linked only by a shared FIXME URL. The PR has no description explaining the failure mode (pkg_resources removal in setuptools 82) or why each hunk is needed. Commit message should state root cause and justify each change.

synthesis.summary: The panel agrees this is a reasonable temporary CI unblock for setuptools 82 removing pkg_resources, which breaks mmcv 2.1.0's build. The dominant concern, raised by all three reviewers, is that the setuptools<82 cap leaks from CI scripts into core/setup.py's runtime install_requires, contaminating every downstream install with a build-time-only constraint. Secondary concerns cluster around documentation hygiene: an unexplained mmengine downgrade from a pinned git SHA to PyPI 0.10.7 that silently drops a stated torch 2.5 fix, implicit ordering coupling between --no-build-isolation and the setuptools pin, and FIXMEs that lack a revert recipe. Verdict: NEEDS-WORK — fix is acceptable in spirit but must keep the CI hack out of the published wheel and document the revert path.
